articles.title: Cabinet clears sale of 60.72% IDBI Bank stake to Fairfax at Rs 52,878 crore — Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Strategic disinvestment — transfer of control, not just shares. Largest FDI in India's financial sector once completed (govt says); largest strategic disinvestment after Air India. Banking-reform and PSU-privatisation Mains theme.
- **Memorise:** Govt sells 30.48%, LIC 30.24%; retains 15% and 19%. Price Rs 81/share vs Rs 75.99 benchmark. Buyer (Fairfax subsidiary, Canada) still needs RBI fit-and-proper clearance; govt's residual 15% to be sold via the Alternative Mechanism in the open market. Process began with the PIM on 7 Oct 2022.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (banking, disinvestment).
- **Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh "Banking" and "Disinvestment" chapters. *Update:* add IDBI to the strategic disinvestment list (Air India, etc.).

articles.title: DRDO tests Quantum Key Distribution platform on a live network at PXE Chandipur — Science & Technology
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Quantum communication for defence. Eavesdropping disturbs quantum states, so it is detectable; keys then feed classical encryption. Pairs with the National Quantum Mission in a Mains answer on quantum technologies.
- **Memorise:** Tested 14 Oct 2026 at Proof & Experimental Establishment, Chandipur (Odisha), to secure telemetry from artillery/armoured weapon tests. Developed under DRDO's MCC cluster; production partner Bengaluru-based Taqbit Labs (spelled "Tagbit" in some reports). July 2026 field trial: 100-km fibre link Prayagraj–Vindhyachal, QBER 6%, ~5 kbps secure key rate.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech / Internal Security.
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Science & Tech: Quantum" and Physics-optional quantum mechanics (measurement/no-cloning). *Update:* add QKD vs Post-Quantum Cryptography comparison.

articles.title: India's Ramsar sites reach 103: Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP) — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Announced 15 Oct by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav. A "Places in News" and wetland-conservation item.
- **Memorise:** Total 103. Sukhna = Ramsar site no. 2602, man-made reservoir (1958) on the Sukhna Choe, Shivalik foothills, Chandigarh's first Ramsar site. Sauj Jheel = no. 2603, perennial floodplain lake in Mainpuri, UP, an IBA hosting 30,000+ waterbirds; UP now has 14 sites.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment / GS1 Geography.
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Wetlands"; Majid Husain geography. *Update:* refresh Ramsar tally (103) and add the two sites to the map.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India's Ramsar sites rise to 103 — Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, UP) added (announced 15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The Environment Minister announced two new Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention, taking India's tally from 101 to 103. It is a standard Prelims "tally + location" item and links to wetland conservation, the Central Asian Flyway and the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules.

**Key facts:**
- **Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2602; man-made reservoir at the Shivalik foothills, created in 1958 by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe; wintering/stopover site on the Central Asian Flyway. Species cited: Common Pochard (VU), Pallas's Fish Eagle (EN), Black Pond Turtle (EN). First Ramsar site of Chandigarh.
- **Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2603; perennial shallow floodplain lake in the Ganga basin, an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area; hosts 30,000+ waterbirds; habitat for Sarus Crane and Greater Spotted Eagle (both VU).
- Mainpuri becomes the only district with two Ramsar sites (other: Saman Bird Sanctuary, 2019). UP's tally reported as 14.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (wetlands, biodiversity conservation, international conventions).

articles.title: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance — DIPAM): Strategic disinvestment of 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to a Fairfax Financial Holdings entity (CCEA, 14 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The CCEA approved the sale of a 60.72% stake (30.48% GoI + 30.24% LIC) in IDBI Bank to 10955230 Canada Inc., a Fairfax Financial Holdings company, for about ₹52,878 crore. The government calls it the largest FDI in India's financial sector. It is the culmination of the long-running strategic sale (RBI categorised IDBI as a private-sector bank in 2019 after LIC took control in 2018; PCA restrictions applied May 2017–Mar 2021).

**Key facts:**
- Consideration ≈ ₹52,877–52,878 crore; DIPAM Secretary said completion is expected before the end of FY 2026-27.
- Completion subject to regulatory approvals; buyer must make an **open offer to minority shareholders**; Fairfax's existing stake in CSB Bank must be merged into IDBI or exited within two years (per one report).
- Residual public holding: one source says GoI ~15% and LIC ~19% (≈34% together) — *single-source, verify against PIB text.*

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (disinvestment, banking sector reforms, FDI, PCA framework).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) launched at Vanijya Bhawan (15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A data-analytics platform to monitor, analyse and govern India's trade ecosystem, giving a consolidated view of trade performance, export-promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators. It supports evidence-based policy and trade facilitation.

**Key facts:**
- Launched by Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.
- Includes a **SCOMET** (Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) dashboard; Minister asked for regular (even weekly) Inter-Ministerial Committee meetings to clear pending SCOMET applications.
- Analysis at national, regional-authority (DGFT), scheme, product, destination-market and application level; role-based access; three focus areas — trade trends, application pendency, timely issue resolution.
- Same day: Commerce data put April–September 2026-27 exports at **US$476.20 billion**; September merchandise exports up 23.04% y/y to US$44.40 bn (secondary source, verify).

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (external sector, trade facilitation, e-governance); GS2 Governance.

articles.title: Canada's Foreign Minister Anita Anand in New Delhi: CEPA targeted for end-2026 — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The India–Canada reset after the 2023–24 diplomatic freeze is now being run through an economic track (CEPA) plus energy, security and people-to-people ties. Tests bilateral-trade facts and the "middle powers" framing in Mains.
**Key facts:** Visit 13–16 Oct 2026 (India, then UAE); talks with EAM S. Jaishankar (reported as their 11th meeting since Sept 2025). CEPA: fifth negotiating round held in Ottawa earlier in October; both sides aim to conclude by end-2026. Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu leads ~300 business delegates (Canada's largest in 30+ years, per reports). Two-way trade ~USD 30.4 bn (2025); Canada's aim USD 70 bn by 2030. Reports say Modi may visit Canada in December.
**Notebook:** GS2 IR (bilateral).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar — India and North America; Shankar/Laxmikanth not needed. *Nudge:* add an India–Canada timeline box (freeze → reset → CEPA) and cross-link to the India–EFTA TEPA note (5 Oct) as the template for a modern FTA.

articles.title: WMO: El Niño "firmly established" — Oct–Dec Niño 3.4 anomaly forecast near +3.7°C, a record — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** New sub-development on the El Niño thread (our 4 Oct item covered only the monsoon wrap-up): the forecast intensity, the role of a positive IOD, and the drier-than-normal signal over the Indian subcontinent in Oct–Dec. Great Prelims-conceptual and Mains (agriculture, rabi, inflation) material.
**Key facts:** WMO update (8 Oct 2026): El Niño likely to peak around December and persist through Feb 2027 (near-100% likelihood), potentially among the strongest since 1950. Niño 3.4 anomaly +1.6°C (June) → +2.5°C (Aug); Oct–Dec forecast ≈ +3.7°C vs previous record +2.6°C (Nov 2015–Jan 2016). Positive IOD expected to peak in October (≈ +0.5°C). Informal "super El Niño" = anomaly ≥ +2.0°C. Aug 2026 was the hottest August on record. Tamil Nadu gets ~48–50% of annual rain from the Northeast Monsoon, which El Niño often favours.
**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (climatology) / GS3 Agriculture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI Fundamental of Physical Geography — Atmospheric Circulation (ENSO, Walker cell); Savindra Singh. *Nudge:* add a Walker-circulation diagram with El Niño vs La Niña vs IOD phases, and a "Niño 3.4 thresholds" line.

articles.title: NBA releases access-and-benefit-sharing funds from the seed sector as CBD COP17 nears — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** ABS is the Nagoya Protocol principle that users of biological resources share benefits with providers. India's implementation (Biological Diversity Act, 2002) is a frequent Prelims theme, and COP17 (Yerevan, 19–30 Oct) will host the first global review of the Kunming-Montreal Framework.
**Key facts:** NBA disbursed roughly ₹2 crore (reported as ₹2.02 crore) from seed-sector companies to 27 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 UT Biodiversity Councils, allocated by area under cultivation; cumulative ABS disbursed crossed ~₹200 crore (figures differ slightly across reports — an earlier August release was reported as ₹2.82 crore and ₹185 crore cumulative, so cite "over ₹200 crore" only loosely). COP17: 19–30 Oct 2026, Yerevan, Armenia, with CP-MOP 12 (Cartagena, biosafety) and NP-MOP 6 (Nagoya, ABS); agenda includes resource mobilisation, DSI/Cali Fund and the first global review of KMGBF. Funds must be used within a year with utilisation certificates.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (biodiversity governance).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS Environment — Biodiversity Act 2002, NBA/SBB/BMC, Nagoya Protocol. *Nudge:* add the NBA–SBB–BMC three-tier chart and a COP17 "what to track" note (30×30, resource mobilisation, DSI); cross-link to the 8 Oct Nagoya MCQ.

articles.title: PM GatiShakti completes five years: 396 projects worth ₹18.66 lakh crore evaluated — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Infrastructure coordination and logistics-cost reduction. The institutional design (EGoS, NPG, TSU, GIS master plan) is a favourite Prelims target, and it supports Mains arguments on cooperative federalism and project delays.
**Key facts:** Launched 13 Oct 2021. By Aug 2026 the Network Planning Group (projects above ₹500 crore) had evaluated 396 projects worth ₹18.66 lakh crore; 256 sanctioned, 198 under implementation. National Master Plan integrates 1,800+ data layers from 58 central ministries/departments and all 36 States/UTs; now extending to district and social-sector planning. Seven "engines": roads, railways, ports, airports, mass transport, waterways, logistics infrastructure. The Cabinet's recent Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (covered 7 Oct) builds on it — no need to repeat.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (infrastructure).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy — Infrastructure and Logistics; National Logistics Policy 2022. *Nudge:* add GatiShakti → NLP → ITLA as a one-line chain.

articles.title: Ministry of Rural Development: Cabinet extends the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for 2026-27 to 2030-31 and renames it "Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana" (Cabinet, 14 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** Union Cabinet approved continuation of NSAP for five years with an outlay of **₹53,428 crore**, 100% centrally funded so benefits are uniform nationwide. About **3.20 crore beneficiaries** across all 36 States/UTs.
- **Why it matters:** NSAP (launched 15 Aug 1995) operationalises **Article 41 (DPSP)** — right to public assistance in old age, sickness, disablement. The revision widens disability coverage.
- **Key facts:** Disability-pension eligibility threshold cut from **80% to 40%** (aligned with RPwD Act, 2016); minimum age condition removed (eligibility from birth); reported assistance ₹375/month (up to 79 yrs) and ₹625/month (80+) *(amounts single-source)*. Old-age, widow and family-benefit components continue unchanged. Revised guidelines due within three months.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance (welfare schemes, vulnerable sections); Polity (DPSP).

### Scheme-in-focus: NSAP → Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
- **Ministry:** Rural Development (Centrally Sponsored; fully Central funding per release).
- **Objective:** Social pension/assistance to poor households (BPL) — old age, widowhood, disability, death of breadwinner.
- **Components (new names):** IGNOAPS → PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana; IGNWPS → PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana; IGNDPS → PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana; National Family Benefit Scheme → PM Parivar Labh Yojana.
- **Coverage:** ~3.20 crore beneficiaries, all States/UTs.
- **Significance:** Rights-based disability inclusion; Article 41 in practice; scheme rebranding trend (cf. VB-G RAM G replacing MGNREGA).

articles.title: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying: India approves accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA) (14 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** India moves from **Cooperating Non-Contracting Party (CNCP, since 2022)** to full participant in SIOFA, a regional fisheries management treaty for non-highly-migratory high-seas stocks in the Southern Indian Ocean.
- **Why it matters:** Indian-flagged vessels can be authorised to fish SIOFA stocks (squid, toothfish, alfonsino); India gets a vote in the Scientific and Compliance Committees and can join the High Seas Boarding & Inspection scheme. Linked to the Guidelines for High Sea Fisheries (Dec 2025) and Blue Economy goals.
- **Key facts:** SIOFA signed in Rome 7 Jul 2006, in force 2012; covers fish, molluscs, crustaceans and other non-highly-migratory species. Tuna (highly migratory) is handled by IOTC, of which India is a member.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy/Environment (Blue Economy, fisheries); GS2 IR (global commons, UNCLOS framework).

articles.title: First BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi adopts the "Delhi Declaration" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India's "Neighbourhood First" and Act East converge in BIMSTEC, and the new Home Ministers' track gives the grouping a security pillar (India is lead on security). It also tests the SAARC-vs-BIMSTEC comparison and Myanmar-conflict constraints.
**Key facts:** Held 13 Oct 2026, chaired by Amit Shah; seven members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand). Mechanism mandated at the 4th Summit (Kathmandu, 2018), welcomed at the 6th (Bangkok, Apr 2025). Declaration: condemns cross-border terrorism, backs UNSC 1267 sanctions, targets scam centres/"cyber slavery" and trafficking (victim-centred SOP), drug-offences monitoring desk, early finalisation of conventions on extradition and trafficking. Bangladesh sent a senior-secretary-led delegation, not its Home Minister. BIMSTEC: Bangkok Declaration 1997; Secretariat Dhaka; Charter in force 2024.
**Notebook:** GS2 IR (regional groupings) / GS3 Internal Security.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar — BIMSTEC; Shankar/Laxmikanth not needed. *Nudge:* add a BIMSTEC "security pillar" box (JWG-CTTC, 2021 counter-terror convention) and cross-link to the SAARC comparison table.

articles.title: PFAS "forever chemicals" in Indian water: studies flag contamination, India has no drinking-water limit — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** An emerging-pollutant explainer: persistent, bioaccumulative, linked to Stockholm Convention listings. Prelims favours convention-listing and IARC-class facts; Mains favours the regulatory-gap argument.
**Key facts:** Chennai study (IIT-Madras, 2024): treated water carried 5–103% more of eight target PFAS than raw water; Visakhapatnam study (2026): 38 of 77 PFAS detected. IARC: PFOA Group 1, PFOS Group 2B. Stockholm Convention: PFOS (2009), PFOA (2019), PFHxS (2022). US EPA limit 4 ng/L for PFOA and PFOS (2024); the Indian standard IS 10500:2012 has no PFAS limit. (Figures from an aggregator summary of the studies; verify against the papers before citing.)
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (pollution).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, Environment — Pollution and International Conventions (Stockholm/POPs). *Nudge:* add PFAS to the POP list with listing years.

articles.title: ICMR to set up its first High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research Centre at Keylong — Science & Technology (Health)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Health research infrastructure for Himalayan and Armed Forces populations; ties to the high-altitude physiology and climate-sensitive disease themes.
**Key facts:** At Keylong (HQ of Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh); foundation stone scheduled for 12 Oct 2026 with Union Health Minister JP Nadda (one source reports it as laid); built by ICMR with the Armed Forces Medical Services and the HP government; research areas include high-altitude physiology, mountain medicine, climate-sensitive diseases, maternal and child health, telemedicine and drone-based health logistics. ICMR: founded 1911 as the Indian Research Fund Association, renamed 1949.
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Health).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / health notes — Biomedical research institutions. *Nudge:* add ICMR centres to the "institutions" table.

articles.title: Ministry of Culture: HAL–National Culture Fund–ASI Memorandum of Agreement for conservation of Hampi, Taj Mahal and Bekal Fort (13 Oct, Kartavya Bhawan-02, New Delhi)
articles.text:
**What it is:** A tripartite MoA under which Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (a defence PSU) gives in-principle CSR-style funding of **₹23.60 crore over 2026-27 to 2028-29** for conservation, preservation and visitor amenities at **Hampi (Karnataka), Taj Mahal (Agra, UP) and Bekal Fort (Kerala)**. ASI provides technical guidance and supervises execution. Signed in the presence of Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal.
**Why it matters:** Continues the shift to public-private/corporate participation in monument conservation, routed through the **National Culture Fund (set up 1996 under the Ministry of Culture)**, which channels donations with tax benefits.
**Notebook:** GS1 Art & Culture (heritage conservation); GS2 Governance (PPP / CSR in culture).

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: Khet Bachao Abhiyan — Rabi-season nationwide soil-health campaign, 22 Oct – 30 Nov 2026 (announced at the PMDDKY one-year review; single-source)
articles.text:
**What it is:** A nationwide campaign promoting balanced fertiliser use (N:P:K per soil and crop need) and curbing excess urea; the ministry has reported lakhs of farmers joining the campaign so far. *(UPDATE — the campaign itself began earlier in 2026; new is the dated Rabi-season run.)*
**Why it matters:** Urea is over-applied vs the benchmark N:P:K ratio of 4:2:1 because its farm-gate price is statutorily fixed, while P&K fertilisers are under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS, since April 2010). Linked tools: Soil Health Card (2015) and PM-PRANAM (2023; States get 50% of subsidy saved as grant).
**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture (inputs, subsidies, soil health).

articles.title: Retail inflation hits a 23-month high of 5.54% in September — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Food and fuel are driving a firmer price cycle just five days after the RBI's repo hike to 5.50%. It tests CPI composition, the 4% (±2) target band, and the monetary-policy link. Note the new-series versus back-series caveat in comparisons.
**Key facts:** CPI 5.54% (Aug revised 4.83%); food (CFPI) 7.74% vs 5.97%; onion inflation 108.09%; rural 6.08%, urban 4.88%; core 4.6%; Tamil Nadu highest state at 6.81%. RBI sees ~6% in Oct–Dec and 5.2% average for FY27; another hike is widely expected at the 2–4 Dec MPC.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy.
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy — Inflation & Monetary Policy chapter. *Nudge:* add a "CPI vs WPI vs core" table and a Sept-2026 data row; cross-link to the MPC note.

articles.title: IPCC meets in Addis Ababa, split over when the Seventh Assessment Report should land — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Climate-science governance. Many European states want AR7 approved before the 2028 global stocktake; Saudi Arabia, China and India are among those seeking 2029 so developing countries get time to review. Deadlock was already visible at IPCC-64 (Bangkok, March 2026). Reports indicate India also withdrew its offer to host COP33 (2028) — single-source report, treat with caution.
**Key facts:** IPCC established 1988 (WMO + UNEP); HQ Geneva; chair Jim Skea; the US reportedly left the body earlier this year; the plenary was under way this week and the outcome was not yet reported at the time of writing.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (climate governance) / GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, Environment — Climate Change chapter (IPCC, UNFCCC, Paris stocktake). *Nudge:* add an "AR7 timeline dispute" box and cross-link to India's CBDR-RC stand.

articles.title: Pakistan declares emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspends the PTI-led government — International Relations (Neighbourhood)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Civil–military and federal–provincial tensions next door, with spillover on terrorism and the Afghanistan frontier. India-relevant for border security and the Pakistan policy debate; it also compares neatly with Article 356 and state emergencies at home.
**Key facts:** Announced 11 Oct 2026 on federal cabinet recommendation, approved by President Zardari; initial six months; Governor to run the province with an advisory council; CM Sohail Afridi reported arrested; PTI called it "a coup disguised as emergency". The trigger was PTI's planned Islamabad march demanding Imran Khan's release.
**Notebook:** GS2 IR (India and neighbours).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar — Pakistan; Laxmikanth, Ch. 'President's Rule' for the Indian comparison. *Nudge:* add a one-line "KP = borders Afghanistan, Durand Line" map note.

articles.title: TRISHNA: ISRO says the Indo-French thermal-infrared satellite is in the advanced stage of realisation — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A bilateral space mission for water stress, crop health and heat mapping, and the third joint India–France satellite after Megha-Tropiques and SARAL.
**Key facts:** CNES supplies the thermal-infrared (TIR) payload; ISRO the VNIR-SWIR payload and bus; launch on PSLV expected in 12–16 months (Wikipedia lists a target of Oct 2027); orbit is sun-synchronous at ~761 km and land resolution ~57 m (secondary source; the revisit figure is inconsistent across sources).
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Space).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / ISRO notes — Earth-observation missions. *Nudge:* add TRISHNA to the India–France cooperation table.

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses — one year on (PIB backgrounder, 11 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** The Mission (Cabinet-approved 1 Oct 2025, launched 11 Oct 2025) aims to end India's chronic pulses import dependence by 2030-31 through area expansion (esp. rice-fallows), certified seed, assured procurement and processing capacity. The one-year backgrounder reports production, area and yield gains in 2025-26 and a sharp fall in imports.

**Key facts / figures:**
- Outlay ₹11,440 crore, 2025-26 to 2030-31 (six years). Focus crops: **tur, urad, masoor**. Cluster approach in **489 districts**; add ~35 lakh ha, aiming for 310 lakh ha area.
- **100% procurement** of tur, urad and masoor at MSP by **NAFED and NCCF**, 2025-26 to 2028-29; 1,000 pulse processing units (dal mills); 87.5 lakh free seed kits and 126 lakh quintals certified seed over six years.
- 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimates): production 274.09 lakh tonnes (from 256.83); area 286.46 lakh ha; yield 957 kg/ha (from 926); procurement up ~70.7% to 31.41 lakh tonnes.
- Trade: imports fell 31.52% in value (₹46,427.60 cr → ₹31,793.59 cr); exports rose 13.4% to ~US$969.5 million.
- 2030-31 targets: ~350 lakh tonnes production, 1,130 kg/ha yield. MSP 2026-27: tur ₹8,450, urad ₹8,200, masoor ₹7,000.
- Delivery gaps: 528 of 1,000 dal mills allocated so far; only 9.25 lakh seed kits distributed in Rabi 2025-26.

**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture (pulses, MSP, food security, import substitution).

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY) completes year one (PIB backgrounder, 10 Oct; anniversary 11 Oct 2026) *(UPDATE — scheme/State rollout was mentioned earlier in the CA; new here are the year-one results and monitoring architecture)*
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** An aspirational-district-style model for agriculture: 100 low-performing districts get a convergence-driven District Action Plan. The year-one data show average scores rising sharply — a template for outcome-based, data-driven governance.

**Key facts / figures:**
- ₹24,000 crore a year for six years from 2025-26 (Cabinet 16 July 2025; launched 11 Oct 2025); ~1.7 crore farmers; **100 districts**, at least one per State.
- Converges **36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries/Departments** plus State schemes and private sector. Selection: low productivity, low cropping intensity, low credit.
- Six objectives: productivity, crop diversification, post-harvest storage, irrigation, credit, governance/service delivery.
- Governance: **District Samiti** (chaired by DM/Collector) prepares the District Action Plan; **State Samiti** (Chief Secretary) reviews; **National Executive Committee** (Union Agriculture Minister); National Monitoring Committee (Secretary, DA&FW).
- Monitoring: **121 indicators** (74 output, 47 outcome), monthly district ranking; dashboard on the NITI Aayog portal. Average score 18.85 (Apr 2026) → 46.89 (Aug 2026).
- Top districts reported: Nagaur (Rajasthan), Gaya (Bihar), Umaria (Madhya Pradesh). DPE has listed adopting these districts as CSR for CPSEs in FY 2026-27 and 2027-28.

**Scheme in focus — PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana:** *Ministry:* Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare. *Objective:* raise productivity and incomes in 100 lagging agricultural districts. *Features:* (i) convergence of 36 schemes; (ii) District Action Plans; (iii) 121-indicator monthly monitoring; (iv) CSR/private participation. *Beneficiaries:* ~1.7 crore farmers. *Significance:* outcome-based convergence governance; blueprint for district-level agri planning.

**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture; GS2 Governance (convergence, aspirational-district model).

articles.title: RBI creates a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) and slashes unhedged derivative limits — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 10 Oct 2026 the RBI tightened rupee FX-derivative rules to curb speculation and keep the market orderly. Authorised Dealers must now hold **cash with the RBI equal to 20% of the rupee notional** on qualifying rupee FX derivative contracts above **US$2 million** that hedge current-account exposures where users buy foreign currency against the rupee. Daily reporting via CIMS; splitting trades to dodge it is a violation. Separate circular cuts the limit on FX derivative positions with **no underlying exposure from US$100 million to US$5 million**, including on exchanges.
**Memorize:** 20% | >$2 mn | $100 mn → $5 mn | held daily till contract ends | an administrative (not rate) tool — contrast with the 7 Oct repo hike to 5.50%. *Outcome sources agree on figures; fuller effective-date wording to be checked against RBI circulars 25 & 26.*
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Monetary/External sector).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Economy — *Forex market, forwards/futures/options, FEMA*; Ramesh Singh — *External Sector*. **Nudge:** add "FERR (2026)" under macro-prudential tools next to CRR/SLR.

articles.title: Parliamentary panel (chair: Shashi Tharoor) calls India's tech-diplomacy "fragmentary and ad hoc" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A report reported on 10 Oct 2026 urges the MEA to publish a **public technology vision document** linking technology to foreign policy, create an **inter-ministerial body for technology diplomacy**, revise India's AI strategy, and publish verified data on data-centre capacity. Useful Mains fodder on tech as an instrument of foreign policy (chips, AI governance, critical minerals, digital public infrastructure).
**Memorize:** Committee = Standing Committee on External Affairs (chair Shashi Tharoor); 3 asks: vision document, inter-ministerial body, verified data-centre numbers. Recommendations are **not binding** — government replies with an Action Taken Report. *(Reported via a news summary; the full report was not checked.)*
**Notebook:** GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — *Parliamentary Committees*; Shankar/Vision IR notes — *Technology diplomacy / India's foreign policy instruments*. **Nudge:** link with India's AI Impact Summit and critical-tech partnerships (iCET/TRUST-type frameworks).

articles.title: Forest Rights Act review: tribal affairs ministry pushes records integration and PVTG habitat rights — Society
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Ministry of Tribal Affairs' regional review conferences on the FRA 2006 (first held in Bengaluru, 10 Sep 2026; the Kolkata conference on 9 Oct 2026 per reports) prioritise integrating forest-rights records with revenue/forest records, strengthening Gram Sabha capacity, and district-level action plans for pending and rejected claims plus **habitat rights for PVTGs**. The review message: measure outcomes by functioning community management, not title counts.
**Memorize:** FRA 2006 — individual rights, community rights, **Community Forest Resource (CFR) rights**, **habitat rights for PVTGs / pre-agricultural communities**. Process: **Gram Sabha → Sub-Divisional Level Committee → District Level Committee (final)**. A national FRA portal is still under development.
**Notebook:** GS1 Society / GS2 Governance (tribal welfare), also GS3 Environment (community conservation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS — *Environment: Forest Rights Act 2006, Gram Sabha*; Laxmikanth — *Fifth/Sixth Schedule, PESA 1996*. **Nudge:** add a "CFR vs habitat rights" comparison table and cross-link to PESA and the Wildlife Protection Act.

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences 2026: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Awarded "for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation." Their work rebuilt macro models on the behaviour of households and firms that plan ahead, so central-bank communication about future policy (forward guidance) shapes expectations — directly relevant to the MPC, inflation targeting and the RBI's recent move to "calibrated tightening."
**Memorize:** Robert E. Hall (Stanford), Michael Woodford (Columbia); prize = Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel (est. 1968, not an original Nobel prize); announced 12 Oct 2026.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (monetary policy).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh — *Monetary policy, MPC, inflation targeting*; Mrunal — *RBI & transmission*. **Nudge:** add "forward guidance / expectations channel" to the monetary-policy notes.

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: Centre urges States/UTs to ensure prominent display of healthcare service rates at clinical establishments (12 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** Union Health Secretary wrote to the Chief Secretaries of all States/UTs asking them to ensure that rates for services and facilities at clinical establishments are displayed at conspicuous, easily accessible places; to review compliance; to issue advisories; and to encourage display of **package rates for international patients on Medical/Ayush visas**.
- **Why it matters:** Price transparency lets patients estimate costs and reduces billing disputes — a patient-rights and federalism question (health is a **State subject**, so enforcement rests with States/UTs).
- **Key facts:** Legal basis — **Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010** and **Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules, 2012**. Where the Act applies, rates for each service/facility must be displayed in **local language and English**; elsewhere State/UT frameworks govern.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance / Health; GS2 Federalism.

articles.title: Ministry of Science & Technology (DST — Technology Development Board): TDB signs agreement with Peptris for ₹86 crore RDI support for AI-driven drug discovery (12 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** TDB-DST and Peptris (AI drug-discovery company) signed an agreement providing ₹86 crore of **Research, Development & Innovation (RDI)** support to speed up AI-led discovery of next-generation therapeutics.
- **Why it matters:** State support for AI × biopharma; TDB is the statutory body that funds commercialisation of indigenous technology. (Funding scheme and therapeutic focus are not stated in the retrievable PIB text — not assumed.)
- **Notebook:** GS3 Science & Tech / Biotechnology.

## Scheme-in-focus: **PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS-NMP)**

- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry (DPIIT — Logistics Division as secretariat of the NPG/EGoS framework).
- **Objective:** Integrated multimodal infrastructure planning on a single GIS platform.
- **Key features:** (1) geospatial data layers from ministries/States; (2) NPG appraisal of projects (ITLA now to appraise ₹500 crore+ projects and prepare a 10+ year National Transport Master Plan); (3) ULIP/API integration of logistics systems; (4) Query-Based Analytics opened to the private sector (Oct 2025).
- **Coverage:** 58 Ministries/Departments, 36 States/UTs.
- **Significance:** Reduces cost/time overruns and logistics cost; supports the National Logistics Policy.

## Also worth a line (12 Oct, headline-level from PIB listing, details not verified)

- PM-SETU: Shareholders' Agreements signed for **Surat and Visakhapatnam** clusters; **₹440 crore** sanctioned for upgrading **nine ITIs** (scheme covered 8 Sep and 4 Oct).
- Ministry of Coal: coal stocks at power plants stay above 18 MT.
- Services athletes felicitated for a record 27 medals at the 2026 Asian Games (overall result covered 7 Oct).

articles.title: USTR opens a comment docket on the EU's CBAM — and asks whether "enforcement action" is warranted — International Relations / Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** CBAM is the sharpest friction between climate policy and trade rules; even the US is now questioning it, which strengthens India's CBDR-RC and WTO-compatibility argument and its India–EU FTA talking points. Expect Mains on "unilateral carbon border taxes".
- **Key facts:** Notice published 8 Oct 2026 (docket USTR-2026-0661); written comments due ~30 days after publication (≈ 7 Nov by the notice's own formula; press reports cite 9 Nov — verify). Seeks views on CBAM's effects on US producers/exports, on EU proposals to widen scope to downstream steel- and aluminium-intensive goods, and on whether enforcement action is appropriate. No retaliation or Section 301 probe announced. CBAM = Reg. (EU) 2023/956; definitive period from 1 Jan 2026; covers cement, iron & steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen.
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR / GS3 Economy & Environment.
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal — *Climate diplomacy & trade* pillar; Shankar IAS — *Climate Change: UNFCCC principles (CBDR-RC)*. Nudge: add CBAM to your India–EU FTA note with the "US is also objecting" line.

articles.title: Ministry of Education (Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth & Sports): 382nd Report on "Reforms and Strengthening of the National Testing Agency (NTA)" presented (adopted 25 Aug; presented in Rajya Sabha 9 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** The Committee (chair: Mukul Wasnik) examined the NTA after the NEET-UG 2024 irregularities and the 2026 NEET-UG cancellation (original exam 3 May; re-exam 21 June). It recommends making the NTA accountable to Parliament, building a permanent in-house cadre, and moving NEET-UG to computer-based testing (CBT) in stages.
- **Why it matters:** Exam integrity and institutional design of a key national body. The Committee's press-reported view is that procedural fixes alone are not enough. Recommendations are not binding on the government.
- **Key facts (single secondary source, not checked against the PIB text):** NTA handles about 1.2 crore candidates a year; NEET-UG alone is above 22 lakh. 23 of 39 sanctioned posts are filled, all on deputation. Revenue surplus of ₹590 crore (FY19–FY25), proposed for funding about 1,000 government CBT centres. A public registry of blacklisted exam vendors, NTA-owned printing presses and an annual equity audit are suggested. Members also raised statutory status for NTA (it is currently an autonomous body registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860) and concerns that CBT may disadvantage rural and marginalised candidates. The Dr K. Radhakrishnan High-Level Committee made 101 recommendations in 2024, being implemented in phases.
- **Notebook:** GS2 – Governance / Education; Polity (Parliamentary Committees).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: 15th ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Joint Committee meeting, Jakarta (6–9 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** Review of AITIGA, signed in 2009 and in force since 2010. The Joint Committee told sub-committees to speed up pending chapters with time-bound deliverables. India will host the next round, in hybrid mode, in January 2027.
- **Why it matters:** The review is meant to make the pact more trade-facilitative; ASEAN is about 11% of India's global trade (press-reported figure). India's concerns include a large trade deficit with ASEAN and rules-of-origin misuse (background knowledge, not in the reports).
- **Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (ASEAN, Act East); GS3 – Economy (trade).

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare (ICAR): New facilities inaugurated at ICAR–Indian Institute of Agricultural Biotechnology (IIAB), Ranchi (8 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated an admin-cum-school building, the Birsa Munda Multipurpose Hall, the Jaipal Singh Munda Sports Complex and a NEXTGEN breeding facility, and laid the foundation of a ₹119 crore guest house. IIAB is at Garhkhatanga, Ranchi.
- **Why it matters:** Agri-biotechnology research capacity in the eastern plateau; he stressed improved seeds, integrated farming and balanced fertiliser use for Jharkhand.
- **Notebook:** GS3 – Agriculture / Science & Tech.

### Also worth a line (not independently verified from PIB text)
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs: 3rd National Conference on CSR (NCCSR 2026) concluded (IICA); no detail verified.
- Ministry of Cooperation: 9th National Review Workshop held in Bastar (8–9 Oct).
- GST 57th Council: PIB backgrounder of 9 Oct adds process details (refund acknowledgement in 10 days, 90% provisional risk-based refunds, no SCN under ₹10,000) — *update to the 10 Oct item; not re-explained.*

articles.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 goes to Navi Pillay — "peace and international law" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured South African jurist Navanethem (Navi) Pillay, 85, of Indian Tamil origin, for promoting peace and international law and for helping ensure war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. It reads as a statement on the rules-based order. Useful for Mains IR/ethics: accountability, universal jurisdiction, role of international courts.
**Memorise:** 125th Peace Prize; 12 million SEK; ceremony Oslo, 10 Dec. Career: first woman to start a law practice in Natal (1967); defended Mandela; first woman of colour on SA High Court; judge at ICTR (helped establish rape as an act of genocide/crime against humanity); judge at ICC; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights; chaired UN Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory; reported to currently sit on the ICJ.
**Notebook:** GS2 – IR (International institutions)
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth/Shankar IAS – "International Organisations: UN & ICJ" and Mrunal IR pillar "International Law". *Nudge:* add a one-line comparison table ICJ vs ICC vs ICTR; cross-link to "India not a party to the Rome Statute".

articles.title: World Bank's World Development Report 2026: "The Promise of Artificial Intelligence" — Reports & Indices
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Released in New Delhi on 8 Oct (presented by Chief Economist Michael Kremer; launched by IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw with the IndiaAI Mission). Core message: AI can widen access to expertise and lift productivity in medical screening, farming advice and education, but gains depend on electricity, connectivity, compute, data, skills and institutions — a "full-stack" approach. India's AI-driven monsoon forecasts to farmers were cited as a lesson (Ethiopia adopting it).
**Memorise:** WDR = annual flagship of the World Bank; IndiaAI Mission – 7 pillars (compute, foundation-model innovation centre, AIKosh datasets platform, application development, FutureSkills, startup financing, safe & trusted AI). Minister's claims (sugarcane yield +40% in Baramati, TB detection +35%) are not report findings.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Sci-Tech / GS2 Governance
**Static anchor:** Mrunal "Reports & Indices" sheet (add WDR 2026); Spectrum/IT chapter on AI. *Nudge:* link with digital public infrastructure and IndiaAI Mission notes.

articles.title: Pre-COP31 in Nadi, Fiji: India presses balance of adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Pre-COP31 (5–8 Oct) was co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu (leaders' event in Tuvalu) to centre Pacific priorities. COP31 will be at **Antalya, Türkiye, 9–20 Nov 2026**, with **Australia presiding over negotiations** — an unusual split-hosting arrangement. Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav called for equal attention to adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation, upheld CBDR-RC "in letter and spirit", and argued against one-size-fits-all action.
**Memorise:** COP31 dates/venue/presidency above; India's three asks: adaptation parity, finance/tech/capacity-building, CBDR-RC.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (Climate diplomacy) / GS2 IR
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – "UNFCCC, Kyoto, Paris"; Mrunal Environment pillar "COP timeline". *Nudge:* add COP31 row to the COP table and link to Article 6 notes (see JCM, 6 Oct).

articles.title: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways: Sagarmanthan 2026 — 3rd edition of "The Great Oceans Dialogue" (New Delhi, 7–8 Oct)
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS2 International Relations / GS3 Economy (Infrastructure, Blue Economy)**

Organised by MoPSW with the Observer Research Foundation. The PM's message called for a "free, open, secure and rules-based" maritime order. The first edition was in Nov 2024.

- Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 presented as a partnership offer (government estimate: about ₹80 lakh crore investment; top-five shipbuilding goal).
- Agenda tracks: India–EU Green Shipping Corridor; review of the India–Korea shipbuilding and logistics framework; IMEC governance; OECD Blue Economy Scoreboards; African corridors such as Lobito.
- Context figures cited: coastline 11,098.81 km, 12 major ports, about 95% of trade by volume by sea.
- Critical point: India's share of global shipbuilding is below 1%.

articles.title: Ministry of Women & Child Development: Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development (8–9 Oct, Sushma Swaraj Bhawan) — second in the PM's series of departmental summits
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS2 Governance (Centre–State, Welfare) / GS1 Society**

Aimed at cooperative federalism, with the vision "Suposhit, Surakshit and Sashakt Bharat". Participants were Centre and state leaders and officials. The PM was scheduled to address the valedictory session on 9 Oct; its outcomes could not be verified.

- Four themes: reimagining Anganwadi Centres (nutrition and early education); child protection systems; women's safety frameworks; effectiveness of women's empowerment schemes.
- Discussion topics: take-home ration and hot cooked meals quality, Poshan Tracker data quality, ECCE, impact of social media on children.

## Also worth a line (not independently verified from PIB text)
- GST Council: single-source mention of 5% optional GST on EV passenger transport and 5% on e-commerce delivery services by unregistered persons.
- Pre-COP31 (Fiji) and MoSPI Environmental-Economic Accounts Strategy: covered in the 9 Oct briefing, no new development found.

articles.title: INS Surya: India's first indigenous Fleet Support Ship launched at HSL, Visakhapatnam — Internal Security
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Defence Minister launched FSS-1 INS Surya, designed and built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (a Defence Ministry PSU). Fleet support ships carry out at-sea replenishment, extending naval endurance and reach in the Indian Ocean Region. It is an Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence example. Reports mention helicopter-deck and self-defence features. *Tonnage and order size are inconsistent across sources, so do not memorize them.*
**Memorize:** FSS = underway replenishment ship | HSL, Visakhapatnam | first indigenously designed and built FSS.
**Notebook:** GS3 Internal Security (Defence indigenisation).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / defence notes on the Navy's blue-water capability. *Nudge:* add under "Navy platforms" and cross-link to the IOR strategy (SAGAR/MAHASAGAR) notes.

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026: optogenetics — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were honoured for optogenetics, in which genetically targeted cells are controlled with light through channels such as channelrhodopsin, first found in algae. It is a tool for mapping neural circuits and for brain-disorder research. Physics (IceCube) and Chemistry (chirality) were covered earlier this week, so this completes the science trio.
**Memorize:** Deisseroth, Hegemann, Nagel | light-gated ion channels (channelrhodopsin, from algae) | genetic targeting + light.
**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (Biotechnology).
**Static anchor:** Biotechnology / genetic engineering chapter of your science notes. *Nudge:* add "Optogenetics" next to CRISPR and gene therapy, and note it as a research tool rather than a therapy.

articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on accessibility in air travel for persons with disabilities — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Per The Hindu (8 Oct), the SC issued notice to the Ministry of Civil Aviation, DGCA, AAI, CISF and the Digi Yatra Foundation on a plea citing gaps such as missing ambulifts, inaccessible in-flight systems and silent airports, and an alleged offloading of a wheelchair user. The petition estimates over 7 million disabled air passengers a year (using the 2011 Census figure of 2.21%). Constitutional hooks: Article 21 (dignity), Article 14, Article 41 (DPSP) and the RPwD Act, 2016 (accessibility provisions). *This is a notice, not a verdict; follow the next hearing.*
**Key facts:** RPwD Act 2016 recognises 21 disabilities; benchmark disability is at least 40%; 4% reservation in government posts. India's domestic air traffic grows about 10–12% a year (per petition).
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity/Governance (vulnerable sections, judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth – Ch. on Fundamental Rights (Art. 21) and DPSP; Social Justice notes on RPwD Act. *Nudge:* add a PIL case-study line under "judicial activism in welfare".

articles.title: Ministry of Textiles: Development Council for Textile Industry (DCTI) holds first meeting (6 Oct, New Delhi) *(single secondary source citing PIB)*
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A consultative council chaired by the Secretary, Textiles, to guide the sector on production and productivity, R&D, exports, raw-material supply, investment, skilling and sustainability; working groups will be formed on priority themes. Reflects institutionalised industry–government consultation.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (industry)

articles.title: Great Nicobar: SC won't stay Calcutta HC hearings; "preservation of culture is a fundamental right" — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 5 Oct a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to interfere with the Calcutta HC order upholding maintainability of a PIL alleging Forest Rights Act violations (consent of tribal communities) in the project. Justice Bagchi's oral remark: protecting the Shompen's identity, not forcing integration, is a constitutionally protected right. A live test of development vs tribal rights vs ecology.
**Memorize:** Shompen = PVTG; HC next hearing 25–26 Nov; two earlier NGT proceedings exist; FRA 2006 requires gram sabha consent.
**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance (also GS1 Society, GS3 Environment).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — Fundamental Rights (Arts 21, 29) + Scheduled & Tribal Areas; *Update:* add "Great Nicobar 2026 – culture as a right" under Art 29(1) and link to PVTG list.

articles.title: First international cargo from Bogibeel: Brahmaputra trade route reopens — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 5 Oct Sarbananda Sonowal flagged off barge DLB Patkai (tug Kushal Konwar) carrying 540 MT methanol from APCL, Namrup to Dhaka region via NW-2 and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. Reported as the first cargo from Upper Assam to a foreign port since 1947; ties to Act East, NE connectivity and Bangladesh relations.
**Memorize:** ~768 km on NW-2, ~1,300 km total; NW-2 = Brahmaputra, Sadiya–Dhubri; NW-1 = Ganga, Prayagraj–Haldia.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Infrastructure/Logistics); GS2 IR (Bangladesh).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh/Shankar — Transport: Inland Waterways; Spectrum Geography — Brahmaputra; *Update:* add 2026 Bogibeel cross-link to the National Waterways list.

articles.title: Delhi High Court: a valid visa is not a right of entry — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** On 1 Oct 2026 Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed a Turkmenistan national's plea after she was denied entry, holding that visa issue and permission to enter are separate and officers keep discretion on grounds like national security, foreign policy and document mismatches. A neat peg for the citizen–alien distinction in fundamental rights and the executive's sovereign power over entry.
**Memorise.**
- Visa gives permission to apply for entry; the final decision rests with the immigration officer.
- Petition failed due to mismatched personal details and no business documents for the stated purpose.
- Constitutional frame: Article 21 (and 14) apply to all "persons"; Article 19 freedoms, including residence and settlement, are for citizens only.
- Reported statutes: the court spoke of the statutory immigration framework; the exact Act cited was not confirmed in my sources.

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth "Fundamental Rights" and "Citizenship". *Nudge:* add a "rights of persons vs citizens" table and this case as a one-line example.

articles.title: Poompuhar's seabed gives up a Mediterranean wine jar — Ancient History / Art & Culture
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The third phase of underwater exploration at Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam), by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology with the Indian Maritime University, ended on 22 Sept 2026. The finds corroborate Sangam-age maritime trade with West Asia and the Mediterranean and show a submerged city. A natural fit for GS1 (Sangam Age, Indo-Roman trade) and Prelims "ports" questions.
**Memorise.**
- A West Asian torpedo-jar fragment (30–35 cm), used to carry wine and olive oil.
- Over 250 ceramic pieces, four terracotta ring wells; read as a buried palaeochannel swallowed by the sea (about 4th–5th century CE).
- Tools: side-scan sonar, sub-bottom profiler, multibeam, ROVs.
- Poompuhar = Chola port at the Cauvery mouth; other sites to pair: Arikamedu, Alagankulam, Muziris/Pattanam.

**Notebook:** GS1 Ancient History and Art & Culture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Old (R.S. Sharma) "Sangam age"; Nitin Singhania "Ancient trade". *Nudge:* update your ports table (Poompuhar–Chola, Korkai–Pandya, Muziris and Tondi–Chera) with this find.

articles.title: Monsoon 2026 closes at 87% of LPA — the driest since 2015, and the east is the worst hit — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** IMD's season summary (30 Sept): 759.4 mm, 87% of LPA, 4th lowest since 2001. The new angle versus the drought-watch item of 25 Sept is the full-season map: Central India was normal, while East/North-East and the South Peninsula were badly short. A model Mains case for El Niño years and regional variation.
**Memorise.**
- Seasonal: 759.4 mm = 87% of LPA (the IMD 'deficient' band is below 90%).
- East and North-East India 74% (lowest since 1901); South Peninsula 76%; North-West 94%; Central 97%.
- Monthly: June 65%, July 101%, August 84%, September 92%.
- Kerala onset 4 June (3 days late); withdrawal began 19 Sept; 17 of 36 subdivisions deficient, only Odisha in excess.
- Strong El Niño influence reported.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI "India: Physical Environment", Ch. 4 Climate; Mrunal Geography pillar, "Monsoon mechanism". *Nudge:* add a "monsoon 2026" data box to your El Niño and IOD notes.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: Two male Great Indian Bustards released into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer (4 Oct) *(UPDATE — the 3 Oct briefing covered the process being initiated; what is new is the actual first release of two captive-bred males.)*
articles.text:
- **What:** PIB: the Union Environment Minister released **two male** Great Indian Bustards (GIBs) into the wild at Desert National Park — the first actual release in the recovery programme, culminating about ten years of effort (Project GIB, 2016).
- **Why it matters:** Moves from ex-situ breeding to in-situ rewilding; post-release survival (power lines, predators, habitat loss) will decide if the programme works. See the 3 Oct note for the programme background (captive breeding since 2019, "jump-start" egg-swap technique, rewilding tunnel).
- **Static link:** GIB — IUCN *Critically Endangered*, Schedule I WPA 1972, CMS Appendix I, Rajasthan's State bird.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment (species conservation).

articles.title: Places in News — Kaliningrad: Putin's "all weapons" warning — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** On 1 Oct 2026 at the Valdai Forum Putin said Russia would use "all the weapons at our country's disposal" if Kaliningrad were attacked. Reports say NATO also received a Russian diplomatic note on a possible nuclear response if the exclave is cut off. Kaliningrad's location, as a non-contiguous Russian territory on the Baltic between Poland and Lithuania, is what makes it a standing flashpoint. Map-based questions are likely.
**Memorise.**
- Kaliningrad Oblast: Russian exclave on the Baltic coast between Poland and Lithuania, with no land link to mainland Russia.
- Baltic Fleet HQ at Baltiysk.
- The Suwałki Gap (the Poland–Lithuania land strip between Kaliningrad and Belarus) is the NATO-side pressure point.
- NATO chief Rutte responded that the alliance is defensive.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (Places in News); links to GS2 IR (Russia–NATO).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / NCERT "World map – Europe & Baltic"; Mrunal "World Geography – Baltic Sea". *Nudge:* add Kaliningrad, the Suwałki Gap, Baltiysk and the Baltic states to your Europe map sheet.

articles.title: Rajasthan High Court warns Jaipur's Walled City could lose World Heritage status — Art & Culture
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** In a suo motu case, the Rajasthan HC (order of 26 Sep 2026) said the Walled City faces a "serious risk" if remedial action is not taken by December 2026. It ordered a survey of unauthorised construction (two weeks), an affidavit on safeguards (four weeks), and a phase-wise action plan, and asked why officials should not face action. UNESCO has flagged redevelopment in the core and buffer zones; the conservation report is due in December 2026 and review is expected at the 2027 World Heritage Committee session (per Outlook Traveller, March 2026).
**Memorize:** Jaipur Walled City inscribed 2019 (founded 1727). The World Heritage Committee decides on the List of World Heritage in Danger and on deletion. Tools: Heritage Impact Assessment, buffer zone, Reactive Monitoring. Only a handful of sites have ever been delisted globally.
**Notebook:** GS1 Art & Culture (Heritage conservation); GS2 Polity (judicial activism).
**Static anchor:** Nitin Singhania *Art & Culture* — UNESCO sites; NCERT *Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art*. **Nudge:** add Jaipur to a "WH sites under UNESCO scrutiny" list with Hampi and Ahmedabad as comparators; cross-link to the Ancient Monuments Act (AMASR Act 1958/2010).
*(Note: this is a follow-up on heritage, not a repeat of the 24 Sep UNESCO Tentative List story.)*

articles.title: Supreme Court: no total firecracker ban, no 24-hour bursting — time-limited use is the middle path — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A clean case of the Court balancing fundamental rights against each other: religious and cultural practice (Art. 25) on one side, and health and a clean environment (Art. 21) on the other. It is a strong Mains example of judicial balancing and of the Court as environmental regulator.
**Memorise:** ***Arjun Gopal v. Union of India*** (W.P.(C) 728/2015), bench of **Justices M.M. Sundresh and Augustine George Masih**. The Court said it would not agree to a **total ban** and would not allow **unrestricted use**, and signalled **specified bursting hours** and limits on cracker types during festivals. It approved manufacture of **new-generation joint (series) crackers** subject to conditions (shell size and quantity limits, intervals between bursts) based on **CSIR-NEERI** specifications. **Barium** content in **Generation-2 green crackers** is being tested in **Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai**; the decision is **deferred to 15 Oct 2026**. Delhi-NCR restrictions run in the separate **M.C. Mehta** proceedings. Constitutional hooks: **Art. 21** (health, clean environment), **Art. 25(1)** (subject to public order, morality, health).
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary; Fundamental Rights); GS3 – Environment.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Fundamental Rights → Art. 21 and Art. 25*. *Nudge:* add "No total ban; time-bound use; barium test decision 15 Oct 2026" under your Art. 21 environmental-rights case list, and cross-link to the GRAP item above.

articles.title: Ministry of Steel: Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) set up as an apex safety body, backed by a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (28–30 Sep)
The Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for the Supreme Court — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** This is the first batch of elevations since Parliament raised the Court's strength to 38. It also brings the appointment machinery back into focus: the Judges Cases, the Memorandum of Procedure, seniority and diversity.
**Memorise:** On **28 Sept 2026** the Collegium (**CJI Surya Kant** with Justices Vikram Nath, B.V. Nagarathna, M.M. Sundresh and P.S. Narasimha) recommended **Justice Sunita Agarwal** (CJ, Gujarat HC; parent HC Allahabad), **Justice D.K. Upadhyaya** (CJ, Delhi HC; from Allahabad) and **Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh** (CJ, Telangana HC; parent HC Jharkhand). The SC's working strength is **34 against a sanctioned 38**. If these three are appointed, it becomes **37 with one vacancy**. The strength went from 34 to 38 (CJI + 37) through the **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026**, which got presidential assent on 12 Aug 2026 and replaced the May 2026 Ordinance. Justice Agarwal would make **three women judges** on the SC. None of the three is in line to become CJI. *Mains line:* "Adding benches only helps if appointments keep pace. Sanctioned strength means little without timely elevations."
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Supreme Court* chapter → Composition (Art. 124(1): Parliament fixes the number by law) and Appointment of Judges (the Judges Cases). *Nudge:* change "34" to "38 (2026 Amendment Act)" in your notes and add this batch as a live example beside the Second/Third/Fourth Judges Cases.

articles.title: Jaishankar's UNGA-81 statement: the Indus Waters Treaty goes on the UN record, and India co-founds a shipping-safety group — International Relations
articles.text:
**What's new since the 21 Sept preview:** India delivered its national statement on **26 September 2026**. Two things in it are new for your notes. India defended keeping the **Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance** from the UNGA podium. India also joined **Liberia** and about two dozen partners to launch a **Group of Friends on the Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers**.

**Exam angle:** This is India's first statement at the General Assembly that ties a water treaty directly to cross-border terrorism. The line was that "friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism", and that understandings premised on good faith "will naturally be called into question". For Mains, use it on how far treaty obligations stand when there is a security threat (IR / GS2). The shipping group adds to India's maritime-security material alongside the Red Sea attacks, SAGAR/MAHASAGAR and the IMO.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Speech: 26 Sept 2026, 81st UNGA General Debate. Lines to quote: "Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised". He called Pakistan a "serial practitioner of terrorism".
- IWT stays **in abeyance** (in place since April 2025, after Pahalgam) "until Pakistan … credibly and irrevocably ends its support for cross-border … terrorism".
- **IWT basics:** signed **1960, Karachi**, by **Nehru and Ayub Khan**, with the **World Bank** as a signatory. **Eastern rivers** (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) go to India. **Western rivers** (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) go to Pakistan, and India has limited non-consumptive uses such as run-of-river hydro. Disputes pass through the **Permanent Indus Commission**, then a Neutral Expert, then a Court of Arbitration.
- Shipping: "the targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers … is simply unacceptable". **Liberia** is one of the world's largest flag-registries, so a flag state is co-leading the group.
- Other lines from the speech: the "**4F crisis**" in the Global South (food, fuel, fertiliser, finance); "endless war must give way to an end to war" (on Ukraine).

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — IR (India–Pakistan; Important international groupings). GS3 link: water security.

**Static anchor:** Your GS2 India–Neighbourhood file (India–Pakistan → IWT). Cross-link to *Spectrum / NCERT Geography — Indus river system*. **Nudge:** add a box showing "IWT: Eastern vs Western rivers + three-tier dispute ladder", and link it to the 21 Sept UNGA card.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: Interest-free working capital of ₹50,000 per barn for FCV tobacco farmers in Andhra Pradesh
articles.text:
On **25 September 2026**, the Centre approved an **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme** for **Flue-Cured Virginia (FCV) tobacco** growers in **Andhra Pradesh**. The government linked the move to weaker global demand, geopolitical developments and shifts in international trade. About **100 million kg** of FCV tobacco had been auctioned in the **2025-26 season**, which opened on **25 March 2026**.

**Why it matters:** This is a textbook conflict for Mains. Farm-income distress in a crop whose exports earn foreign exchange sits against India's public-health commitments under the **WHO FCTC**. Article 17 of the FCTC asks parties to promote economically viable alternatives to tobacco growing.

### Scheme-in-focus: **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme (FCV tobacco, Andhra Pradesh)**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce). Tobacco is a commercial crop regulated by the **Tobacco Board** (a statutory body under the Tobacco Board Act, 1975, headquartered in **Guntur**).
- **Objective:** Give immediate liquidity to growers hit by slow sales in a weak market.
- **Key features:** (i) **₹50,000 per curing barn**, **interest-free**; (ii) paid by **DBT** into farmers' accounts; (iii) meant for repaying institutional loans, household needs and next-season inputs; (iv) aims to cut dependence on private moneylenders.
- **Beneficiaries/coverage:** About **44,000 farmers**, with a total outlay of about **₹220 crore**.
- **Significance:** A targeted, time-bound liquidity measure rather than a price support. Useful as an example of how trade shocks pass through to farm incomes.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Agriculture (commercial crops, farm credit); cross-tag GS2 Health (FCTC).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (DPIIT): Make in India completes 12 years — PIB stocktake of manufacturing, FDI and PLI outcomes
articles.text:
Make in India was launched on **25 September 2014** to turn India into a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. On its 12th anniversary, the government put out a consolidated scorecard, and the Prime Minister summed it up as "more made in India, more investment, more exports".

**Why it matters:** This is the government's own balance sheet for its flagship industrial policy. Mains questions on deindustrialisation, PLI effectiveness and "Make in India vs. import dependence" need these baseline numbers. The release also shows the policy's new shape: sector-specific incentives such as PLI, semiconductors and rare-earth magnets now sit on top of the original ease-of-doing-business agenda.

**Key facts**
- Now called **Make in India 2.0**, it covers **27 sectors (15 manufacturing + 12 services)**.
- **Cumulative FDI of about US$ 843 billion** from 2014-15 to 2025-26.
- **Electronics production** rose from **₹1.9 lakh crore (2014-15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025-26)**. India is the **world's 2nd-largest mobile phone manufacturer**.
- **Defence production** rose from **₹46,429 crore (2014-15) to ₹1.78 lakh crore (2025-26)**. **Crude steel** rose from **81.7 MT to 170 MT**, and India has been the 2nd-largest producer since 2018.
- **PLI schemes** cover **14 sectors**. Reported production and sales exceed **₹22 lakh crore** and jobs exceed **14 lakh** (sources give slightly different cut-off figures).
- Enablers: the **National Single Window System** (327 Central + 3,452 State approvals), the **India Industrial Land Bank** (4,220 parks mapped), **PM GatiShakti** and **Startup India** (about 2.54 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups).

### Initiative-in-focus: **Make in India**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry, through **DPIIT**. **Launched:** 25 September 2014.
- **Objective:** Promote investment, foster innovation, build skills and create world-class manufacturing infrastructure.
- **Key features:** (i) four pillars: new processes, new infrastructure, new sectors and a new mindset; (ii) liberalised FDI, with the automatic route in most sectors; (iii) regulatory simplification through NSWS and ease-of-doing-business reforms; (iv) since 2020, sector-specific **PLI schemes** plus semiconductor and electronics-component missions.
- **Coverage:** 27 sectors under Make in India 2.0.
- **Significance:** Measures both the *scale* of output gains (electronics, defence, steel) and the *open questions* around domestic value addition and manufacturing's share of GDP. Use it to write a balanced Mains answer.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (industrial policy, manufacturing, FDI).

articles.title: The World Circular Economy Forum opens in Gandhinagar — its 10th edition and its first in South Asia — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline.** WCEF 2026 runs **15–18 September at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar**, on the theme *"Circular economy: Transition for people and prosperity"* — convened by Finland's **Sitra** with the **Central Pollution Control Board**, supported by MoEFCC and the Gujarat government. Over 2,000 participants from 65-plus countries; 125-plus exhibitors. The Board of the **10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP)** meets at Gandhinagar on 15 September, with India having recently taken over as **Co-Chair**.

**Exam angle.** Circularity is the connective tissue between SDG 12, the plastics-treaty negotiations, critical-mineral security and Mission LiFE — a single Mains paragraph can carry all four. The examiner's favourite distinction is **recycling (end-of-pipe, still linear) vs circularity (design-stage: durability, repairability, reuse, remanufacture)**, and the Indian policy instrument that operationalises it is **Extended Producer Responsibility**, which UPSC has already asked about directly.

**Facts to memorise.**

- WCEF launched by **Sitra (the Finnish Innovation Fund) at Helsinki in 2017**; 2026 is the **10th edition**, the first in South Asia.
- **10YFP** — the SCP framework adopted at **Rio+20 (2012)**, secretariat with UNEP; India now Co-Chair of its Board.
- India's architecture: **NITI Aayog's 11 circular-economy committees (March 2021)** across municipal solid and liquid waste, scrap metal, Li-ion batteries, tyres and rubber, gypsum, end-of-life vehicles, e-waste, hazardous industrial waste, used oil, agricultural waste and solar panels.
- EPR is embedded in the **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2022)**, **E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022** and **Battery Waste Management Rules 2022** — but was *first introduced* in the **e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011**.

**Notebook.** GS3 — Environment (Pollution & waste management) with a GS3 Economy spillover on resource security.

**Static anchor.** Shankar IAS *Environment* — Pollution / Waste Management chapter. *Update:* add the 11 NITI focus sectors as a memorised list, and cross-link EPR to the three waste rules plus the 2019 PYQ.

articles.title: Acharya Vinoba Bhave's birth anniversary — the land-reform movement that worked morally and failed statistically — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Prime Minister paid tribute to **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** on his **birth anniversary (11 September)** — born **Vinayak Narahari Bhave, 11 September 1895 – 15 November 1982** — the Gandhian who was hand-picked as India's **first individual Satyagrahi in 1940** and who launched the **Bhoodan movement in 1951**.

**Exam angle:** This is a **post-independence GS1 topic** that UPSC has asked in Mains verbatim (see the PYQ mirror), and the examinable argument is the gap between **moral success and structural failure**. Bhoodan was a **voluntary, non-legislative** alternative to state-led land redistribution: Bhave walked village to village asking landowners to gift land, and from **1954** escalated to **Gramdan**, the donation of whole villages into common ownership. The movement collected roughly **42 lakh acres**, but only a fraction was ever distributed — much of it was **litigated, uncultivable, or reverted** when Gramdan villages drifted back to individual title. The reason to know the numbers is that they let you make the argument precisely: voluntary transfer could not overcome **absentee landlordism, benami holdings and defective land records** — which is exactly the diagnosis that statutory **land-ceiling legislation** and, much later, **land-records digitisation** were meant to address. That gives you a live cross-link to **DILRMP 3.0** (12 September note). The second thread is **ideological**: Bhoodan is the practical arm of **Sarvodaya** and of Gandhi's **trusteeship** doctrine, and its political afterlife runs through **Jayaprakash Narayan**, who left party politics for Sarvodaya in 1954 and returned in 1974 with **Sampoorna Kranti** — a chain worth writing in one line.

**Facts to memorise:**

- **Vinayak Narahari "Vinoba" Bhave**, b. **11 September 1895**, Gagode village, **Raigad district, Maharashtra** (Konkan); d. 15 November 1982. Gandhi gave him the name **Vinoba**, placing him in the lineage of **Jnanoba and Tukoba**. Met Gandhi at **Ahmedabad, 7 June 1916**.
- **First individual Satyagrahi**, selected by Gandhi to launch the **Individual Civil Disobedience Movement, October 1940**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the second. Gandhi introduced him publicly through the essay ***"Who is Vinoba?"***
- **Bhoodan (land-gift) movement:** launched **18 April 1951** at **Pochampally village, Nalgonda district** (then Hyderabad State, now **Telangana**), where **Vedre Ramachandra Reddy** donated **100 acres** to landless Harijan families. **Gramdan** (village-gift) followed from **1954**; the first Gramdan village was **Mangroth (Uttar Pradesh)**.
- **Institutions:** **Sarva Seva Sangh** and the **Akhil Bharat Sarva Seva Sangh** carried the movement; **Gram Seva Mandal, Wardha (1934)**; earlier, the **Nagpur Flag Satyagraha (1923)**.
- **Writings:** ***Geetai*** (the Bhagavad Gita in Marathi verse, 1930–31); ***Gita Pravachane*** (18 talks delivered in **Dhule jail, 1932**); *Swarajya-Shastra*; *Sthitaprajna-Darshan*.
- **Honours:** first international **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership (1958)**; **Bharat Ratna, posthumously in 1983**.
- **Contrast to hold ready:** Bhoodan = **voluntary and moral**; **land-ceiling laws** = **statutory and coercive**, and many were placed in the **Ninth Schedule** to shield them from judicial review.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern Indian History and post-independence consolidation (social reformers; land reforms), with a GS4 spillover (trusteeship, moral persuasion as an instrument of change).

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum / Bipan Chandra — the post-independence land-reforms section; NCERT Class XII *Politics in India Since Independence*, Ch. 3 ("Politics of Planned Development").** *Update:* build a single **land-reforms ladder** — *Zamindari abolition (1950s) → Tenancy reform → Bhoodan–Gramdan (1951/1954, voluntary) → Land-ceiling legislation + Ninth Schedule → Consolidation of holdings → DILRMP/SVAMITVA (records, 2008–)* — and mark against each whether it was **voluntary or statutory** and **why it under-delivered**. **Cross-link** to your **Ninth Schedule / *I.R. Coelho* (2007)** note in Laxmikanth and to the **DILRMP 3.0** entry from 12 September.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change: India to host the World Circular Economy Forum 2026 at Gandhinagar, 15–18 September
articles.text:
India will host the **World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026** for the first time — and the first time the forum comes to **South Asia** — at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, on the theme **"Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity."** WCEF is the flagship global circular-economy convening initiated by **Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund**; the 2025 edition was held in São Paulo, Brazil. India had declared its candidacy at the 12th Regional 3R and Circular Economy Forum in Jaipur.

**Key facts**

- **Dates/venue:** 15–18 September 2026, Gandhinagar, Gujarat.
- **Co-organisers:** MoEFCC, **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, Sitra (Finland), Government of Gujarat and the **Gujarat Pollution Control Board**.
- **Scale:** over **2,000 stakeholders from 65+ countries**; an exhibition with **125+ national and international exhibitors** showcasing start-up and investment-ready circular solutions.
- To be inaugurated on 15 September by Union Environment Minister **Bhupender Yadav** with the Gujarat Chief Minister.
- India's circular-economy potential has been officially pegged at a market value of **over $2 trillion and close to 10 million jobs by 2050**.

**Why it matters:** Links directly to Extended Producer Responsibility rules (plastic, e-waste, battery, tyre, used oil), **Mission LiFE**, the Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy agenda, and India's positioning as a Global South convener on sustainability.

**Notebook:** GS3 — Environment (waste management, resource efficiency); GS2 — IR (India as Global South convener).

articles.title: Rani Avantibai Lodhi gets a statue in Lucknow — the 1857 revolt beyond the four famous names — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline.** Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh**, with UP Chief Minister **Yogi Adityanath**, unveiled a statue of **Veerangana Rani Avantibai Lodhi** in **Lucknow on 30 August 2026**, drawing a line from the 1857 warrior queens to women officers who flew combat roles in Operation Sindoor.

**Exam angle.** UPSC's 1857 questions have moved steadily away from Delhi–Kanpur–Lucknow and toward **regional centres and their leaders** — exactly the space Avantibai occupies. Her case is also the textbook illustration of a **doctrine that is not the Doctrine of Lapse**: her husband died leaving **minor** heirs, so the Company did not annex Ramgarh outright — it placed the estate under the **Court of Wards** and installed *sarbarahkars* (superintendents), a mechanism used for minor or "incompetent" heirs. That is a distinction students routinely get wrong, and it is precisely the sort of thing a statement-based Prelims question exploits. Avantibai expelled the Company's administrators, called on cultivators to refuse British revenue demands, and coordinated with the **Gond ruler Raja Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla** through the famous **bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring chiefs and zamindars, taunting them to fight or accept the bangles. She won at the **Battle of Kheri** near Mandla against Deputy Commissioner Waddington in 1857, then shifted to guerrilla operations from the **Devhargarh** hills, and took her own life on **20 March 1858** at Sukhi-Talaiya rather than be captured. Her Mahakoshal base — Gond and farming country — is the entry point for the **tribal dimension of 1857**, which is separate from and usually more useful than the sepoy narrative.

**Facts to memorise.**

- **Maharani Avantibai Lodhi**, **16 August 1831 – 20 March 1858**; queen-regent of the estate of **Ramgarh** (present-day **Dindori and Mandla districts, Madhya Pradesh**); born at **Mankedi village, Seoni district**.
- Married **Raja Vikramaditya Singh of Ramgarh**; assumed regency for minor sons **Aman Singh** and **Sher Singh** when he was incapacitated.
- Mechanism of British seizure: **Court of Wards** with **sarbarahkars** — not the **Doctrine of Lapse** (which applied to rulers dying *without* a natural heir).
- Ally: **Raja Shankar Shah**, Gond ruler of **Garha-Mandla**, executed by the British at Jabalpur in **September 1857** along with his son **Raghunath Shah** (blown from a cannon).
- **The bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring rulers and zamindars as a challenge to join the revolt.
- **Battle of Kheri** (near Mandla, late 1857) — roughly **4,000 troops** defeated the force under Deputy Commissioner **Waddington**.
- Retreat to the **Devhargarh** hills; guerrilla strikes; encircled at **Sukhi-Talaiya** between Balapur and Ramgarh; **martyrdom on 20 March 1858**, aged 27.
- Group her with the other *veeranganas*: **Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi)**, **Jhalkari Bai** (Lakshmibai's Durga Dal commander), **Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh)**, **Rani Durgavati** (16th-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga — *not* 1857; a standard trap), **Uda Devi (Sikandar Bagh)**.
